variants.note: Own hard constraint c01: 'A gabled principal roof... disqualifies the node.'
Craftsman's device, not Prairie's; own c01 disqualifies a gabled principal roof outright.

roof_form.rule: Principal roof hipped at 3:12 to 4:12; a gabled principal roof disqualifies the node (own hard constraint c01).
roof_form.note: Overrides the parent's deliberately-open gable/hip pairing with Prairie's own documented and hard-constrained answer -- specified directly here (not left to cascade) so this node's provenance is its own c01, not an accidental agreement with a distant Palladian-villa ancestor several links away in the arts-and-crafts-british lineage chain, which was the pre-fix source for this exact value.

roof_pitch.rule: Principal roof hipped at 3:12 to 4:12 (own hard constraint c01) -- narrower than the family's shared 3:12-6:12 band.
roof_pitch.note: Narrows the family's own roof_pitch (3:12-6:12) to Prairie's own tighter, hipped-only figure.

variants.note: Own hard constraint c02: 'The eave soffit is a continuous closed plane,' and own diagnostic_tells: 'The eave soffit is clean: no rafter tails, no knee braces, no brackets. This is the fastest separation from Craftsman.'
Craftsman's device, explicitly forbidden by own c02.

projection_in.note: Own defining_characteristics: eaves projecting 30 in to 48 in.

eave_condition.rule: Exposed rafter tails, knee braces, applied brackets, shutters, and any classical or revival ornament are forbidden; the eave soffit is a continuous closed plane (own hard constraint c02).
eave_condition.note: Resolves the family's own deliberately-open eave_condition branch (exposed-rafter-tails vs closed-soffit) to Prairie's own documented answer.

rake_condition.rule: The rake carries the same closed, continuous soffit plane as the eave; no bargeboard, exposed purlin, or knee brace of any kind.

gable_treatment.rule: There is effectively no gable to treat: the principal roof is hipped throughout (roof_form, above), so no gable wall arises for ornament to occupy.
gable_treatment.note: Follows directly from the node's own hipped-roof requirement (c01).

dormer.rule: No dormer interrupts the continuous hipped roof plane and eave band; a dormer would break the unbroken horizontal lines (fascia, lintel band, sill band, water table) the node's own c03 requires to return unbroken around every corner.
dormer.note: Not stated explicitly by name, but follows directly from the node's own emphasis on the roof reading as 'an unbroken floating plane' and c03's continuous-band requirement; no exemplar or description mentions a dormer anywhere in the node's own text.

chimney.rule: The chimney is a massive central masonry mass about which the plan pinwheels, visibly the fattest and heaviest object in the composition, terminating above the highest roof plane (own hard constraint c05).
chimney.note: Directly grounded in defining_characteristics #4 and diagnostic_tells ('The chimney is visibly the fattest object in the composition and the plan turns around it') and own hard constraint c05.

compressed_ceiling_ft.note: Own typical_ratios: 6 ft 10 in to 7 ft 4 in at compression (entry, circulation).

released_ceiling_ft.note: Own typical_ratios: 9 ft 0 in to 10 ft 0 in at release (living space).

height_proportion.rule: Ceiling heights are deliberately differentiated between compressed circulation and released living volume rather than held constant storey to storey.

variants.note: Own diagnostic tell: brick roughly twice as long and half as tall as standard, laid with raked horizontal and flush vertical joints so only the horizontal reads.
The Craftsman-lineage material; Prairie's wall is continuous and unornamented, not a textured natural-shingle field.

primary_cladding.rule: Wall surfaces are continuous and unornamented: stucco with wood banding, or long thin Roman brick in raked horizontal joints (own defining_characteristics).

water_table.rule: The water table is one of the four continuous horizontal bands (own c03); it must return unbroken around every corner.

belt_course.rule: A continuous water table, sill course, lintel course, and fascia are drawn unbroken around the whole building -- four horizontal lines that must return around every corner without interruption (own hard constraint c03).
belt_course.note: Directly grounded in own c03 and defining_characteristics #2.

corner_quoin.rule: No quoin or masonry corner relief occurs; corners are dissolved with glass or turned by a projecting pier, never articulated by a classical masonry device.
corner_quoin.note: Follows from the node's own long description ('Corners are dissolved with glass or turned by a projecting pier') and the family-level corner_quoin prohibition, restated here for provenance since Prairie diverges from the Craftsman-lineage corner_board answer entirely.

corner_board.rule: The corner is either dissolved in continuous glazing or turned by a projecting masonry pier; there is no applied board at all.
corner_board.note: Overrides the family's own 'plain-board' answer (the Craftsman-lineage device) with Prairie's own corner treatment, directly quoted above.

cornice.rule: No projecting classical cornice occurs; the fascia is one of the four continuous horizontal bands (belt_course, above), not an entablature member.

variants.note: Own diagnostic tell: 'Casement windows in continuous ribbons.'
Craftsman's own device; Prairie's is the casement band.

window_type.rule: Windows are casements gathered into continuous horizontal bands.
window_type.note: Overrides the parent style's own double-hung binding, which is correct for the Craftsman lineage but wrong here.

window_lite_pattern.rule: Art glass is rectilinear geometric with no curves, its pattern derived from the plan's own geometry (own diagnostic tells: 'art glass in rectilinear geometry and no curves').
window_lite_pattern.note: Overrides the parent's 'multi-light-over-single-light' double-hung pattern, which does not apply to a casement band.

window_grouping_rule.rule: The compositional unit is the continuous band, not the individual sash; window bands run 3 to 8 casement units of roughly 1 ft 10 in to 2 ft 4 in each, and solid wall occurs between bands rather than between windows.
window_grouping_rule.note: Directly grounded in the node's own proportional_system.typical_ratios and bay_rhythm.

porch_type.rule: There is no habitable-depth porch of the Craftsman kind; where a sheltered outdoor space occurs it is a low terrace or a porte-cochere integrated into the horizontal massing, not a room framed under a subordinate gable.
porch_type.note: Not stated as a prohibition explicitly, but no exemplar or description in the node's own text mentions a porch; the family's own porch_type binding (specified for the Craftsman lineage) is explicitly wrong here since it presupposes a gabled roof continuation this node's own c01 forbids.

entry_sequence.rule: Arrival is a sequence rather than an announcement: the entry is displaced, often around a corner or behind the chimney mass, and approached at right angles to the direction of arrival; the primary entry may not be centred on the principal street elevation (own hard constraint c04).
entry_sequence.note: Directly grounded in defining_characteristics #5, diagnostic_tells ('You cannot find the front door from the sidewalk'), and own hard constraint c04.

circulation_parti.rule_append: The plan pinwheels about the central chimney mass rather than opening toward a single hearth wall, and Wright's own stated programme was to 'eliminate the attic, the cellar stair, the porch spindle, the bric-a-brac, and the room-by-room subdivision of the ground floor.'

hearth_position.rule: The hearth sits within the massive central chimney about which the plan pinwheels -- the tallest and heaviest element of the composition -- not at a gable end and not paired.
hearth_position.note: Overrides the family's Georgian-derived gable-end-paired hearth answer with Prairie's own central-mass answer.

orientation_rule.rule: The entry is approached at right angles to the direction of arrival rather than square-on (own hard constraint c04); orientation otherwise follows the site's own geometry.
